meta.name: Signal catalogue — how to generate useful signals, and which ones this data can actually support
meta.definition: A signal is a rule that maps information available before kickoff to a probability. A signal is useful only if it is (a) computable from a named source, (b) available before the decision cutoff, and (c) calibratable with n and uncertainty.

tiers.T1-computable-now: Every input is ingested from an official source and the signal can be computed with published n and interval today.
tiers.T2-computable-after-one-more-source: One named official source is missing; the gap is stated.
tiers.T3-not-computable: Requires information that is not published by any official source; listed so it is not attempted.

meta.killerRule: Any signal whose input arrives after the decision cutoff is not a signal — it is a leak. That is why publication time, not just content, is part of every input definition.

signals.name: Exact rest days
signals.definition: Days between a team's previous official kickoff date and its next one.
signals.input: Official kickoff date per game (nfl.com by-week pages).
signals.availability: Published with the schedule, months before kickoff.
signals.limitation: Does not adjust for travel or for a bye beyond the rest count itself.

signals.name: Short-week indicator
signals.definition: Flag when rest <= 4 days (a Thursday game after a Sunday game).
signals.limitation: Small number of Thursday games per season, so the sample stays tiny for years.

signals.name: Scoring rate, shrunk
signals.definition: Points scored and allowed per game, each shrunk toward the league mean by a fixed weight so an 8-game sample cannot look like a 17-game truth.
signals.input: Official team scoring stats (offence and defence, all 32 clubs).
signals.leakRisk: Low — but the page is 'season to date', so a mid-season historical backtest must use archived pages, not today's numbers. Using today's page to test a week-3 game is a leak.
signals.limitation: League-mean opponent adjustment is crude; a proper opponent-adjusted rating needs play-by-play.

signals.name: Pass/run efficiency split
signals.definition: Yards per attempt and yards per carry, offence and defence, as a two-factor profile.
signals.input: Official team passing/rushing stats, offence and defence.
signals.limitation: Rate stats without opponent adjustment and without garbage-time filtering overstate blowout teams.

signals.name: Turnover differential (defence side)
signals.definition: Interceptions and fumble recoveries per game, defence side, as a regression candidate.
signals.input: Official team defence passing stats (interceptions) and defensive scoring columns.
signals.limitation: The official team pages do not publish a single turnover-differential column; it must be assembled from the defensive columns and labelled as assembled.

signals.name: Injury load by unit
signals.definition: Count of players listed Out / Doubtful / Questionable on the official report, split by offence and defence, using the official report's own positions.
signals.input: Official NFL injury report, latest published week.
signals.availability: Published during the week; final game-status update 90 minutes before kickoff per NFL rules.
signals.leakRisk: HIGH. If a bet is placed before the final update, the later update is a leak. The site therefore stamps the report's week and never mixes weeks.
signals.limitation: A count is not a value: three Questionable backups matter less than one Out quarterback. The count is published as a count, with the positions listed, never as a severity score.

signals.name: Depth-tier exposure
signals.definition: For each club, how many published tiers exist at each position, and which tier the official injury report suggests is next up.
signals.input: Club depth charts (1st/2nd/3rd/4th) joined to the official injury report.
signals.availability: Club charts carry their own 'updated as of' date; those dates differ across clubs.
signals.leakRisk: Medium — a chart updated after the bet is a leak. The chart date is shown next to every row so staleness is visible.
signals.limitation: Charts are club projections; several clubs label them 'Unofficial'. A depth chart is not a snap count (Q07).

signals.name: Player usage stability
signals.definition: Game-to-game standard deviation of a player's attempts/receptions relative to his mean — a stability score, not a forecast.
signals.leakRisk: None for a historical description; using the full season to forecast week 5 is a leak.
signals.limitation: Below the suppression floor of 8 games the score is withheld.

signals.name: Teammate dependence
signals.definition: Correlation between two teammates' weekly volumes (QB passing vs WR1 receiving), which is the input a same-game parlay needs.
signals.input: Two official per-game logs joined by week and opponent.
signals.leakRisk: None historically; the forecast version must use only prior weeks.
signals.limitation: Needs both players' logs on the same club for the same weeks; the join rate is published, unmatched rows are excluded and counted.

signals.name: Home-field prior
signals.definition: The realised home-team win rate over the loaded official finals.
signals.limitation: A prior, not an edge. Published with n so its uncertainty is visible.

signals.name: Travel distance
signals.definition: Great-circle distance between a team's home city and the venue.
signals.input: Official venue per game (present) + venue coordinates (not published by the NFL).
signals.availability: Venue is official; coordinates are not.
signals.limitation: Adding a coordinate list means adding a non-official source. That is a decision for the owner, not a silent import.

signals.name: Actual participation / snap share
signals.definition: Whether the nominal backup actually played and how much.
signals.input: Needs the official snap-count or gamebook publication.
signals.leakRisk: High if used retrospectively without an archive.
signals.limitation: Without it, 'the 2nd string replaced the starter' is an inference from a depth chart, not a fact.

signals.name: Weather
signals.definition: Temperature, wind and precipitation at kickoff.
signals.input: Needs an official weather source; the official NFL pages publish a short forecast line for some games only.
signals.availability: Inconsistent — a weather line appeared on one probed week page and not another.
signals.leakRisk: Forecast vs actual is a leak if mixed.
signals.limitation: Not uniformly published; only dome/outdoor venue type would be reliably derivable.

signals.name: Market price itself
signals.definition: The de-vigged market probability, which is the strongest known baseline.
signals.input: Needs a licensed or owner-recorded two-way price (Q01).
signals.leakRisk: Closing vs pre-game price must be timestamped or CLV is meaningless.
signals.limitation: Without it, no strategy can be shown to beat anything resembling a market.

signals.name: Referee assignment effects
signals.input: Crew assignments are not published as a machine-readable official feed on the pages probed.
signals.limitation: Listed so nobody spends a session on it. The official rulebook was probed and the 2026 rulebook URL returned 404 — the exact current URL must be found before quoting any rule.

signals.name: In-game live betting signals
signals.definition: Any signal that updates during a game.
signals.input: Needs a live feed with a timestamped tick history.
signals.leakRisk: Total — a live signal cannot be evaluated with post-game data.
signals.limitation: Out of scope until a live feed exists.

combinationRules.rule: Never multiply leg probabilities unless the legs are on different games, different teams and different players, and even then publish the empirical joint as the primary number.
combinationRules.why: Independence is an assumption; the empirical joint is a measurement. When both are available, the measurement wins.

combinationRules.rule: A parlay's price must show the hold compounding: a three-leg parlay at the same hold has roughly three times the margin of a single.
combinationRules.why: Parlays are usually a worse deal per unit staked, and that is a computable fact rather than an opinion. The market page computes it for any stated price pair.

combinationRules.rule: Correlation between legs must be reported with its interval, and a correlation whose interval spans zero must be printed as 'indistinguishable from zero'.
combinationRules.why: With 8 games, almost every correlation spans zero. Saying so is the honest output.

combinationRules.rule: A player-prop combo on one player (e.g. rushing yards over AND receptions over) is a single joint event and must be estimated from that player's joint outcomes, never from two marginals.
combinationRules.why: Same-player legs can be strongly positive or negative depending on game script.
